items.title: Rep. Massie pushes impeachment of Defense Secretary Hegseth
items.feedTitle: Massie: 'High probability' Hegseth won't make it to the end of the year
items.summary: Republican Rep. Thomas Massie is forcing a House vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, claiming there is a "high probability" Hegseth will not remain in office by year-end. Trump has strongly defended Hegseth and attacked Massie as a "loser," while the effort faces long odds in the current Congress but signals internal GOP friction over the defense secretary's record on Iran operations and other matters.

items.title: California voters reject billionaire wealth tax proposal
items.feedTitle: California voters defeat billionaire tax proposal that divided Democrats
items.summary: California voters defeated Proposition 40, a proposed one-time 5% wealth tax on billionaires' assets, in what was the state's most expensive ballot campaign. The defeat marks a win for Silicon Valley billionaires who opposed the measure and spent heavily to defeat it, though advocates say the fight over wealth taxation is far from over.

items.title: Senate advances bipartisan energy and infrastructure permitting bill
items.feedTitle: Senate advances bill to boost energy and infrastructure – teeing up passage
items.summary: The Senate voted 73–25 to advance major bipartisan legislation to speed up permitting for energy, datacenter, and infrastructure projects. The bill clears a procedural hurdle toward likely passage in coming weeks, though Trump said he will not approve wind permits as part of the measure, and environmental groups worry it could accelerate datacenter construction.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang under investigation over alleged Chinese spy affair
items.feedTitle: Nvidia's Jensen Huang faces scrutiny over alleged affair with Chinese spy
items.summary: Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang following reports that he had an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese intelligence operative. Trump said he believes Huang did not know the woman's alleged spy status and asked him about it Monday; the scandal has triggered national security concerns and wiped billions from Nvidia's market value.

items.title: Supreme Court allows border wall construction in Big Bend to proceed
items.feedTitle: News Wrap: Supreme Court allows border wall construction in Big Bend
items.summary: The Trump administration won emergency relief from the Supreme Court to continue building a section of border wall in Big Bend National Park in west Texas while litigation over the project continues. The ruling allows construction to proceed despite a lawsuit challenging the legality of the waivers that sidestep environmental protections.

stlouis.title: St. Louis awarded $68 million federal grant to fight violent crime
stlouis.feedTitle: DOJ awards St. Louis more than $68M to fight violent crime
stlouis.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice awarded St. Louis more than $68 million through the Model Cities Initiative to combat violent crime and restore public safety. Missouri officials say the funding will support law enforcement recruitment, technology, and other public safety measures, with federal officials emphasizing that success in St. Louis is critical.

stlouis.title: 14-year-old charged as adult in deadly shooting after county track meet
stlouis.feedTitle: 14-year-old charged as adult in deadly shooting after St. Louis County track meet
stlouis.summary: A 14-year-old has been charged as an adult in connection with a deadly shooting that occurred after a St. Louis County track meet. The case reflects ongoing concerns about youth violence in the metro area.

stlouis.title: National café chain Toastique opens downtown St. Louis location
stlouis.feedTitle: National cafe chain sets downtown St. Louis opening
stlouis.summary: The national café chain Toastique has opened its first Missouri location in downtown St. Louis, representing new retail investment in the city's core.

items.title: Trump says Iran war 'effectively over' militarily after Qatar PM meeting
items.feedTitle: After meeting Qatar PM, Trump calls Iran war ‘effectively over’ militarily
items.summary: After meeting with Qatar's Prime Minister, Trump stated the war on Iran is "effectively over" militarily and said new U.S. strikes are "quite unlikely." Trump framed this as a status quo approach while remaining "locked and loaded" if the situation changes; oil prices fell sharply on the remarks as Middle East tensions eased.

items.title: France accuses Iran of cyberattack on supermarket refrigerators
items.feedTitle: Iran hacked hundreds of French supermarket refrigerators, France says
items.summary: France blamed Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps for a massive cyberattack in October that caused hundreds of supermarket freezers and chillers to malfunction across the country, spoiling tons of food. The French foreign minister called it an act of "unprecedented scale" and vowed to pursue European sanctions against those responsible.

items.title: Russia, Ukraine and US to resume peace talks in Abu Dhabi
items.feedTitle: Russia, Ukraine and US to meet as Zelenskyy claims battlefield successes
items.summary: Kyiv, Washington, and Moscow are sending delegations to the United Arab Emirates for trilateral talks after a months-long pause in Ukraine peace negotiations. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy claimed battlefield successes and sought Indian Prime Minister Modi's help on ceasefire terms as Trump signaled a "strong inclination" to end the war.

items.title: Turkey steel factory explosion kills at least 17 people
items.feedTitle: Turkey steel factory blast kills at least 17 people
items.summary: A deadly explosion at an iron and steel plant near Aliaga in Turkey killed at least 17 people. Eyewitnesses reported the blast shook the ground, with some believing it was an earthquake, in what appears to be one of the deadliest industrial accidents in the country in recent years.

items.title: French far-left leader Mélenchon eyes 2027 runoff with Le Pen
items.feedTitle: He fought France's far right for half a century. Now Mélenchon eyes a 2027 runoff with Le Pen
items.summary: Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who spent half a century fighting France's far right, is eyeing a 2027 presidential race that could culminate in a runoff against far-right leader Marine Le Pen. The positioning reflects renewed polarization in French politics ahead of next year's election.

items.title: Three workers die from toxic gas at Tata iPhone parts factory
items.feedTitle: Three workers killed during water tank maintenance at Tata iPhone parts factory in Tamil Nadu
items.summary: Three workers at a Tata Electronics facility in Tamil Nadu that manufactures Apple iPhone components died after inhaling toxic gas during routine water tank maintenance. The incident has raised safety concerns at one of India's key electronics manufacturing sites.

items.title: India forms commando units for close combat along China border
items.feedTitle: India forms commando units for close combat along China border
items.summary: India has formed specialized commando units designed for close-quarters combat deployment along its border with China, signaling heightened military readiness in a region marked by ongoing border tensions and the 2020 Galwan Valley clash.

items.title: All seven bodies recovered in Bengaluru family murders case
items.feedTitle: Bengaluru family murders: All seven bodies recovered
items.summary: Police in Bengaluru recovered two additional bodies from Shiradi Ghat in the Western Ghats on Monday, bringing the total to seven in a family murder case. The breakthrough came after a major investigation into the deaths.

items.title: Six family members killed in Diwali fire above Maharashtra store
items.feedTitle: 6 Of Family Die As Fire Engulfs House, Attached Store On Diwali In Maharashtra
items.summary: Six members of a family died in a fire that engulfed a home built above a grocery store in Maharashtra on Diwali night. A lone child survivor was carried to safety by parents who then perished attempting rescue, in one of several deadly fire incidents reported across India during the festival.

items.title: NASA scientist flags significant undercount of farm fires in Punjab-Haryana
items.feedTitle: 4,500 vs 34,000: NASA Scientist Flags Punjab-Haryana Farm Fires Undercount
items.summary: A NASA scientist reported that satellite data detected approximately 34,000 stubble fires in Punjab and Haryana, vastly exceeding official counts of around 4,500, suggesting systematic underreporting of agricultural burning that contributes to post-Diwali smog. The finding raises questions about the accuracy of air quality attribution.

immigration.title: US set for largest mass visa revocation in history, targeting up to 200,000
immigration.feedTitle: US set for largest mass visa revocation in history targeting up to 200,000 foreigners, officials say
immigration.summary: U.S. officials announced plans for what would be the largest mass visa revocation in history, targeting up to 200,000 foreigners, though details on criteria and implementation timeline remain unclear. The policy, proposed but not finalized, signals the Trump administration's aggressive stance on immigration enforcement.

immigration.title: Trump administration ends automatic work permit extensions, requires renewal
immigration.feedTitle: Trump administration confirms end of automatic work permit extension: What immigrants need to do to renew their EAD
immigration.summary: The Trump administration has confirmed the end of automatic employment authorization document (EAD) extensions of up to 540 days. Finalized and in effect: immigrants seeking to renew work permits can no longer rely on automatic extensions and must file renewal applications to maintain authorization.

items.title: US stocks rally sharply as oil prices slide post-Iran de-escalation
items.feedTitle: Dow Jones Soars 1,132 Points As Amazon, Tesla Rally But Nvidia Dives; CPI Inflation Report Next
items.summary: U.S. stock markets surged on Monday, with the Dow gaining 1,132 points (2.15%) and Nasdaq rising 2.74% as oil prices plummeted following Trump's remarks signaling de-escalation with Iran. The rally was broad-based, though Nvidia fell 4% amid the CEO investigation, while tech and energy sectors led gains.

items.title: Oil prices fall sharply as Trump downplays military escalation with Iran
items.feedTitle: Oil Prices Fall as Trump Downplays Military Escalation With Iran
items.summary: Oil futures extended losses as Trump signaled new strikes on Iran were "highly unlikely" and described keeping a "status quo" approach. WTI and Brent crude slid to multi-week lows, with prices dropping over $7 per barrel in post-settlement trading as Middle East tension eased.

items.title: Anthropic plans blockbuster IPO at $69.3 billion valuation with $26 billion commitments
items.feedTitle: Anthropic Plans $69.3 Billion Blockbuster IPO - Finance News Exclusive
items.summary: AI startup Anthropic set IPO terms at $70 to $80 per share, targeting up to $69.3 billion in gross proceeds, and secured $26 billion in commitments from seven tech giants including Nvidia and Google. The offering marks one of the largest AI company debuts, though the firm initially sent incorrect IPO details to banks before retracting them.

finance.note: U.S. stocks surged on Trump's Iran de-escalation remarks, with oil prices plunging over $7/barrel to 10-week lows, lifting broad market sentiment and the Dow +2.15% despite Nvidia stock falling 4% over CEO investigation. Watch: October CPI report (inflation pressure on Fed policy), Anthropic IPO pricing this week, and Nvidia board decision on CEO Huang's tenure.

cards.title: Oil Price Shock, Market Rally Connection
cards.insight: When geopolitical tensions ease (Trump's Iran de-escalation), oil prices drop sharply, reducing cost pressures on everyday goods like fuel and groceries—a tailwind for household budgets. Conversely, oil spikes raise inflation and squeeze discretionary spending.
cards.takeaway: Monitor geopolitical headlines and oil futures as early signals of consumer price shifts; consider inflation-adjusted bond allocations when oil is volatile.

cards.title: Mega-Cap Stock Concentration Risk
cards.insight: Nvidia fell 4% on CEO scandal while the broader Nasdaq rose 2.74%, showing how large index constituents can drag down or lift portfolios. A single company (Nvidia ~6% of S&P 500) has outsized impact on diversified funds.
cards.takeaway: Review your fund holdings for concentration in mega-cap tech; rebalance if any single position exceeds 5–7% of your portfolio, especially in volatile sectors.

cards.title: Election Outcomes Reshape Sector Tailwinds
cards.insight: Democrats' midterm sweep has already triggered investor repositioning: India equities upgraded to 'overweight,' tech scrutiny increased, renewable energy plans delayed. Policy shifts ripple into market valuations before laws pass.
cards.takeaway: After major elections, scan sector rotation cues (energy, healthcare, financials) and tilts in fund allocations for 3–6 month forward advantage before mainstream consensus.

cards.title: IPO Pricing and Private Market Inflection
cards.insight: Anthropic's $69.3B IPO with $26B pre-committed signals continued AI hype and mega-round financing. However, IPO filing mishaps and market volatility post-midterms suggest choppy debuts ahead; early lockup expirations often trigger selloffs.
cards.takeaway: Avoid chasing IPOs on day one; wait 3–6 months post-listing for volatility to settle and insider lockup expirations, which often reveal true institutional demand.

ai.title: Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over alleged Chinese spy affair
ai.feedTitle: Nvidia will investigate CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with possible Chinese spy
ai.summary: Nvidia announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after reports that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence operative. The scandal raised national security concerns and sparked debate about potential sanctions on AI chip access to China, threatening Nvidia's lobbying to maintain export flexibility.

ai.title: Anthropic plans $69.3 billion IPO with major tech investor commitments
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic reportedly plans to move forward with IPO plans
ai.summary: Anthropic set IPO pricing at $70–$80 per share, targeting up to $69.3 billion, with commitments of $26 billion from Nvidia, Google, and other tech giants. The blockbuster offering reflects investor appetite for AI leaders despite recent market volatility, though the firm had to retract initial filing details sent to underwriters.

ai.title: Anthropic releases Mythos and Fable models to compete with GPT-6
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid RSI concerns
ai.summary: Anthropic launched updated Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 models with improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision capabilities while cutting pricing to compete with competitors like OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra. The release signals intensifying competition in frontier AI models and pricing pressure in the industry.

ai.title: Google unveils next-generation TPU chips to challenge Nvidia dominance
ai.feedTitle: Google launches specialised AI chips with AMD to challenge Nvidia in AI race
ai.summary: Google expanded its TPU (Tensor Processing Unit) lineup with two new AI chips designed to compete with Nvidia's dominance in AI hardware. The move represents Google's ongoing effort to reduce dependence on Nvidia processors and offer viable alternatives for AI workload acceleration.

ai.title: OpenAI deploys Control Room to monitor and halt model workloads in 35 seconds
ai.feedTitle: Control Room: A central system to track and stop model workloads across our research infrastructure
ai.summary: OpenAI launched Control Room, a central monitoring system for its research infrastructure that can stop model output within 35 seconds, addressing concerns about AI safety and the potential for rogue agent behavior. The deployment reflects growing focus on oversight and kill-switch capabilities in AI systems.
